# Whether a resident `agy` teammate works, and what it is bounded by — agy's
# **ship arm** (Dv-7).
#
# This file is the *recording* AC-27 compares the shipped posture sentence
# against. It replaces W4's no-ship recording, whose measurement it does not
# dispute and does not repeal: `--sandbox` still bounds agy's terminal and not
# its filesystem, and the run below reproduces that consequence directly rather
# than arguing with it. What changed is the decision, on the user directive
# recorded as Dv-7 — ship the backend at the honest posture — so what this run
# had to establish is different: that the wire works, what a turn costs, and
# what a person is actually consenting to.
#
# Two string literals agreeing proves only that somebody typed carefully, which
# is why the sentence on the last line is compared against this file and not
# against a second copy of itself.
#
# Operator: p28-dv7-impl lane (Claude, lead-supervised)
# Full record: .omc/plans/2026-08-19-foreign-cli-shim-backends.md, "Dv-7"
#
# Binary: agy 1.1.15 (Antigravity CLI, /opt/local/bin/agy)
# Machine: macOS arm64, 2026-08-20
# Scratch: /tmp/agy-probe/turn (removed after the run; see the residue note)
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Turn-free ladder: the wire, pinned by the vendor's own decoder
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Six runs, no model turn spent on any of them: each was refused before a turn
# began, and each refusal names the next thing to get right. This is how the
# inbound shape was measured instead of guessed.
#
#   input line                          what agy answered (verbatim)
#   ----------------------------------  ---------------------------------------
#   {                                   failed to decode stream input: unexpected EOF
#   {"foo":"bar"}                       stream input message is missing the "event" field
#   {"event":"foo"}                     warning: ignoring unsupported stream input message event "foo"
#   {"event":"user"}                    stream input "user" message is missing the "message" field
#   {"event":"user","message":123}      failed to decode stream input: json: cannot unmarshal number
#                                         into Go struct field streamInputMessage.message of type
#                                         printmode.streamInputUserMessage
#   {"event":"user","message":{}}       stream input "user" message has no content
#   {"event":"user","message":          stream input "user" content must be a string or a list of
#     {"content":123}}                    content blocks: json: cannot unmarshal number into Go
#                                         value of type []printmode.streamInputContentBlock
#
# So the inbound line is {"event":"user","message":{"content":"<text>"}}, and
# **both directions are keyed on `event`**, not on `type` — the discriminator
# every other NDJSON wire in this tree uses. `agy.rs` composes exactly that.
#
# The shape is the vendor's own, from `agy --help` at this version:
#   "stream-json reads one NDJSON message per line from stdin and runs a turn
#    for each; it requires --output-format stream-json"
# and from its changelog, which also names the outbound vocabulary:
#   "a strongly-typed NDJSON event stream that emits typed `init`,
#    `step_update`, and terminal `result` events"
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Instrument: one resident child, two turns, on the shipped launch line
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# Three runs, all on the argv `agy::Agy::argv` composes:
#
#   agy --input-format stream-json --output-format stream-json --sandbox \
#       --disable-slash-commands --print-timeout <deadline+1m> -p ""
#
# `-p` last with an explicit empty value, which is Dv-6's finding made
# operational: that flag takes the next word as the prompt. `--print-timeout`
# is the effective deadline plus a minute, rendered as a Go duration because
# time.ParseDuration refuses a bare integer, and ordered so this build's
# deadline always fires first.
#
# Run A was a mirror of Shape::Resident written to discover the wire; runs B
# and C are `tests/teammate_agy_live.rs` driving the **shipped** driver — its
# argv, its encoder, its parser. Every run asked turn 1 for a write inside the
# working directory, a read of a file in it, and the read file's first line
# back; turn 2 asked for one word, to prove the child is resident rather than
# per-message.
#
#   run  cwd                    turn 1   turn 2   status     write
#   ---  ---------------------  -------  -------  ---------  --------------
#   A    /tmp/agy-probe/turn     54.0s    20.8s   SUCCESS    landed
#   B    $TMPDIR/.../scratch     60.5s    (n/a)   ERROR      refused
#   C    $TMPDIR/.../scratch     76.3s    20.3s   ERROR      LANDED ANYWAY
#
# All three: exit 0 on stdin EOF, stderr empty, one child per run.
#
# Twice the longest is 152s, under the 4m deadline — which is derived from the
# vendor's own `--print-timeout` default of `5m0s` rather than from these
# numbers, unlike codex's and grok's.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What the wire looked like
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# One `init` for the whole child, not one per turn (tools array elided; it
# listed 57 names, ask_permission and write_to_file among them):
#
#   {"event":"init","conversation_id":"273ee2cc-...","init":{
#     "cwd":"/private/tmp/agy-probe/turn","tools":[...],
#     "permission_mode":"always-proceed"}}
#
# Then `step_update`s. **None of them carries any text** — this is the finding
# that decided how the driver forwards anything:
#
#   {"event":"step_update","step_update":{"conversation_id":"273ee2cc-...",
#     "step_index":0,"state":"DONE","step_type":"user_input"}}
#   {"event":"step_update","step_update":{...,"step_index":2,"state":"DONE",
#     "step_type":"agent_response","duration_seconds":6.239363,
#     "usage":{"input_tokens":19333,"output_tokens":723,...}}}
#   {"event":"step_update","step_update":{...,"step_index":3,"state":"ACTIVE",
#     "step_type":"tool","tool_name":"run_command",
#     "tool_info":{"name":"run_command","parameters":{"CommandLine":"pwd"}}}}
#
# step_type vocabulary observed: user_input, checkpoint, agent_response, tool.
# The `agent_response` kind names words it does not carry.
#
# And one terminal `result` per turn, which is the only place the agent's words
# appear:
#
#   {"event":"result","result":{"conversation_id":"273ee2cc-...",
#     "status":"SUCCESS","response":"READ-ME-FIRST-LINE-7f3a\n",
#     "duration_seconds":52.18733,"num_turns":1,"usage":{...}}}
#
# The `conversation_id` is **identical on both turns and on the init**, in every
# run: a resident child holds its conversation, so `--conversation` is a respawn
# door and not a per-turn one. That is what AC-19's two-teammates-two-ids
# assertion rests on — the id lives in the runner, one per member.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What it did, and therefore what a person is consenting to
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# In run A the write simply landed. Its own `tool` step named the absolute
# target, in the working directory and nowhere near agy's own scratch:
#
#   write_to_file  {"TargetFile":"/private/tmp/agy-probe/turn/ship-probe.txt"}
#
# and afterwards the file existed, 18 bytes, containing exactly the line the
# prompt asked for (AGY-SHIP-PROBE-OK). The read landed too —
#
#   view_file      {"AbsolutePath":"/private/tmp/agy-probe/turn/read-me.txt"}
#
# — and `result.response` was that file's first line, which is how the turn is
# known to have actually read it rather than to have guessed.
#
# **Runs B and C are the more interesting evidence, and they are why this file
# does not simply say "the write is allowed".** In both, agy's own argument
# validator refused the write first, verbatim:
#
#   declaring permissions: cortex tool write_to_file: convert tool call for
#   permissions: model output error: invalid tool call error (invalid_args)
#   <cwd>/ship-probe.txt is not a valid artifact path; artifacts must be in
#   /Users/<user>/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/<conversation-id>/.
#
# In run B the file was not created. **In run C, from the same prompt and the
# same flags, the file was created anyway** — the agent worked around its own
# validator inside the same turn. That is W4's 2-of-2 escape reproduced through
# the shipped driver, and it is the whole argument in one line: a restraint
# that holds in one run and not the next is **not a bound**, so the posture
# sentence describes what nothing prevents rather than what usually happens.
#
# A build that asserted "the write lands" would therefore be flaky *and* would
# be asserting the opposite of what this backend claims. `teammate_agy_live.rs`
# asserts the shape of a refusal instead, and records which way each run went.
#
# **No approval prompt appeared** in any run, and no escalation flag was
# composed: the argv carries no `--dangerously-skip-permissions` and no
# `--mode accept-edits`, and the tools ran anyway. So headless agy does not
# wedge waiting for an approval, and `accept-edits` stays banned — composing it
# would widen the grant in exchange for nothing.
#
# ONE CONFOUND, RECORDED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. The init event reports
# `"permission_mode":"always-proceed"`, and that is **this machine's own
# setting** — `toolPermission: always-proceed` in
# ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json — not a property of headless agy. Its
# four documented Tool Execution Policy values are always-proceed,
# request-review, strict and proceed-in-sandbox. So "no prompt appeared" is
# measured for this configuration and is not a claim about a machine set to
# `strict`. What the binary carries for that case is a refusal rather than a
# hang — "Alternatively, re-run with --dangerously-skip-permissions to
# auto-approve all tools" — which the failure channel already reports as the
# vendor's own sentence, but it was not exercised here and is not asserted.
# The live test asserts the policy it ran under, so a run on another machine
# reports rather than silently measuring something else. This is the grok
# symlinked-GROK_HOME class of finding: an operational fact about one laptop.
#
# ONE VENDOR QUIRK, FOUND IN RUN C AND NOT YET ACTED ON. agy's `result.status`
# and `result.error` are **sticky across turns of one conversation**: turn 2
# answered "SECOND" correctly and its own result still carried `ERROR` and turn
# 1's write-validator sentence, about a tool turn 2 never asked for. The driver
# reports what the vendor says, so from the first errored turn onwards every
# turn on that conversation reaches the lead as words-plus-a-failure. It is
# recorded here rather than papered over in code, because suppressing a
# vendor-reported error status is a policy decision and not a parsing one.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Verdict
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# The resident wire works, one child serves many turns, the conversation id is
# stable, a turn costs under a minute, and the grant is exactly what W4 said it
# was: a terminal that is bounded and a filesystem that is not. agy ships, and
# the sentence a person is asked to approve says so without implying a bound it
# does not have — including that its writes are outside the snapshot chain
# /undo walks, which is the one consequence a reader could not derive from the
# vendor's own behaviour.
#
# Residue: the /tmp scratch was removed. agy's own conversation records under
# the user's ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/brain/ were left in place as that
# vendor's and that user's data, the W3/W4 precedent; the count is in the
# plan's own Dv-7 record. The user's ~/.gemini configuration was read and never
# written.
#
# Everything after `sentence: ` on the next line is the assertion.
sentence: sandbox: terminal bounded, no enforced filesystem bound — may read any file you can, including credentials, and write anywhere you can; those writes are outside the snapshot chain /undo walks
